C API Reference#

The full C API is defined in these headers:

  • include/ovphysx/ovphysx.h – API functions

  • include/ovphysx/ovphysx_types.h – types and enums

  • include/ovphysx/ovphysx_attributes.h – OVPHYSX_ATTR_* attribute-name macros; include it alongside ovphysx.h, which does not include it

  • include/ovphysx/ovphysx_geometry_query.h – geometry queries (SDF shape evaluation); include it alongside ovphysx.h, which does not include it

  • include/ovphysx/ovphysx_legacy.h – deprecated families (tensor bindings, binding-coupled control, scene queries, contact bindings, SDF views, object-type lookup)

  • include/ovphysx/ovphysx_legacy_types.h – types used only by the legacy header

  • include/ovphysx/ovphysx_config.h – scoped config value builders (ovphysx_config_value_*)

  • include/ovphysx/ovphysx_legacy_config.h – deprecated typed entry builders

C++ convenience wrappers (experimental, C++17):

  • include/ovphysx/experimental/ovphysx.hpp – RAII instance wrapper

  • include/ovphysx/experimental/Helpers.hpp – RAII helpers, including WaitResult

  • include/ovphysx/experimental/OvStageOutput.hpp – application-owned CPU/CUDA world-transform publication in ovphysx::utils; see ovstage integration

  • include/ovphysx/experimental/TensorBinding.hpp – RAII tensor binding wrapper (deprecated; use ovphysx_read / ovphysx_write)

For rendered documentation with full descriptions, refer to the built HTML docs.

C API Functions#

Articulation Kinematic Update#

Use ovphysx_update_articulations_kinematic() after writing articulation DOF positions or velocities when link state must reflect the new generalized state before the next simulation step. Pass a live OVPHYSX_QUERY_TARGET_ARTICULATION query to select the articulations and POSITION and/or VELOCITY flags. The Python method is PhysX.update_articulations_kinematic(), and the experimental C++ wrapper is PhysX::updateArticulationsKinematic(). The C and C++ calls return a task receipt; wait for it before using updated link poses. Python waits internally and returns None, raising any execution failure; its scope argument creates the articulation query. The native operation currently executes inline. It updates articulation forward kinematics only; after any required first GPU warmup, it does not run a normal simulation step or collision/contact processing.

Initialize process-global ovphysx lifecycle state.

Returns:

  • OVPHYSX_API_SUCCESS if lifecycle state was initialized.

  • OVPHYSX_API_ERROR if lifecycle state is already initialized, or on x86_64 if the host CPU or OS does not expose AVX (required by pre-built x86_64 binaries).

ovphysx_result_t ovphysx_create_instance(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t *out_handle,
)#

Create a new instance with default instance configuration.

Set process-global configuration before this call. After creation, instance configuration may be changed with ovphysx_set_config() until the instance attaches a stage.

Parameters:

out_handle – [out] New owned instance handle.

Returns:

OVPHYSX_API_SUCCESS, OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_ARGUMENT when out_handle is NULL, or OVPHYSX_API_ERROR when lifecycle/runtime initialization fails.

ovphysx_result_t ovphysx_destroy_instance(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
)#

Destroy an ovphysx instance and release per-instance resources.

Per-instance destruction leaves the process lifecycle active. Call ovphysx_shutdown after destroying the final handle to drain the direct PhysX runtime and clear that lifecycle token.

#include <ovphysx/ovphysx.h>

static ovphysx_result_t destroy_owned_instance(ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle)
{
    return ovphysx_destroy_instance(handle);
}
Side Effects

Releases internal resources, plugins, and cached data for this instance.

Threading

Do not destroy an instance while it is in use on other threads.

Ownership

After destruction, any bindings created by this instance are invalid.

Errors

  • OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_STATE is retryable: admission rejected before teardown; the handle, attachment and caller ownership remain live. Close companion leases or finish pending work/transitions before retrying.

  • OVPHYSX_API_ERROR if the handle is not registered or destruction fails. An unregistered handle is rejected before teardown and does not affect registered instances or process-global asynchronous state. No error string is returned. Consult logs for other destruction failures.

Parameters:

handle – ovphysx handle to destroy.

Returns:

ovphysx_result_t with status and error info.

Post:

On success, the handle is unregistered and its resources are released. A repeated call for that already-unregistered value returns OVPHYSX_API_ERROR before teardown and has no effect on registered instances or process-global asynchronous state.

ovphysx_result_t ovphysx_shutdown(void)#

Clear the ovphysx process-lifecycle token.

Clears the process-global initialized state set by ovphysx_initialize. It does not destroy live handles and does not balance ovphysx_create_instance. Callers must destroy every handle explicitly with ovphysx_destroy_instance.

Must be paired with a prior ovphysx_initialize call. Call once when the application is done with the current process-lifecycle scope. After shutdown, callers must invoke ovphysx_initialize again before creating another instance.

On every successful return, including when live handles remain, shutdown flushes Carbonite’s buffered records, stops accepting application-callback delivery, and drains accepted callbacks. When runtime teardown occurs, the barrier includes its final log producer. The callback and its user-data resources may then be released. Accepted callbacks must not wait indefinitely on the thread performing shutdown.

Static runtime mode

With no live handles, shutdown drains the direct PhysX runtime. On Linux it also releases the SDK-owned Carbonite framework and private cooking cache. Windows retains the framework until process exit for safe dependency DLL teardown; private cache removal after datastore shutdown is best-effort. A framework populated by a foreign host remains owned by that host. If live handles remain, callers still own them and the direct runtime remains available only for their explicit destruction. Continued stepping or other instance work after shutdown is unsupported, and destruction-time records are not delivered to the application callback disabled by shutdown.

Returns:

  • OVPHYSX_API_SUCCESS on success.

  • OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_STATE is retryable: retained companion service leases still prevent shutdown. The lifecycle token remains live.

  • OVPHYSX_API_ERROR if called without a matching ovphysx_initialize.

  • OVPHYSX_API_ERROR if called from the application log callback. Use ovphysx_get_last_error() for details.

ovphysx_result_t ovphysx_ovd_start_recording(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
const ovphysx_omnipvd_destination_t *destination,
)#

Start an OVD recording session.

The call is synchronous. A FILE destination is an exact path. A TCP destination connects to a ready listener. Validation and stream-open failures may be retried. Only one recording may be active in the shared runtime: another start returns OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_STATE without replacing its destination. After a successful stop, another FILE or TCP session may be started. Late start requires a live physics stage in the shared runtime. Before its first attach and between detach and reattach it returns OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_STATE.

Make the shared runtime OVD recording capable by setting OVPHYSX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_OVD_RECORDING_CAPABLE to true with ovphysx_set_global_config() before the first ovphysx_create_instance(). The key defaults to false. Capability alone does not start recording; attach a physics stage and call this function with the desired destination. Pass ovphysx_config_value_bool(true), declared in ovphysx_config.h. A default, incapable runtime returns OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_STATE with an error naming the capability key. Unsupported platforms retain OVPHYSX_API_NOT_IMPLEMENTED.

Creation and attachment never start recording. After reattach, the runtime remains dormant until this function is called. Call it before the first simulation step to capture the initial state and every simulation frame.

Parameters:

  • handle – Instance requesting the recording session.

  • destination – FILE or TCP destination borrowed for this call.

Returns:

OVPHYSX_API_SUCCESS, OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_ARGUMENT for an invalid destination, OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_STATE when the runtime is not recording-capable, the shared runtime has no live physics stage, or recording is active, OVPHYSX_API_NOT_IMPLEMENTED on an unsupported platform, or OVPHYSX_API_ERROR when the destination cannot be opened or sampling cannot start.

ovphysx_result_t ovphysx_ovd_stop_recording(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
)#

Stop and finalize the active recording.

The handle that started the session owns it. A peer handle is inactive and cannot stop the owner’s session. A successful owner stop permits a later recording session to start.

Returns:

OVPHYSX_API_SUCCESS, OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_STATE when this handle owns no active recording (including while a peer owns the globally active session), or OVPHYSX_API_ERROR when stop/finalization fails.

ovphysx_result_t ovphysx_ovd_is_recording(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
bool *out_is_recording,
)#

Query whether this instance owns the active recording.

A peer reports false while another instance owns the shared runtime’s active recording.

Parameters:

  • handle – Valid instance handle.

  • out_is_recording – [out] Receives true only while sampling is active.

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t ovphysx_attach_ovstage(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovstage_instance_t *stage,
ovstage_ordinal_t read_ordinal,
)#

Attach an ovstage Stage as the orchestration data surface.

Once attached, the orchestration contract is explicit and application-owned in both directions (the application owns ordinal advancement):

  • Application to physics (control in): the application authors dirty control attributes into ovstage (drive:force, drive:velocity, drive:position_target, physics:mass, physics:gravityMagnitude, physics:gravityDirection, and so on) at ordinals it chooses, then calls ovphysx_update_from_ovstage to drain that ordinal range into the running simulation. ovphysx_step then integrates.

  • Physics to application (output out): ovphysx_step does not author simulation output back into the Stage on its own. The application reads the step’s output with ovphysx_read / ovphysx_fetch_read_next and writes it back into ovstage at a separate, higher (physics-output) ordinal. That ordinal is never covered by update_from_ovstage, so physics never reprocesses its own writes. See the ordinal-coupling section on ovphysx_query.

This is one consistent model: initial parse at attach, explicit control updates via update_from_ovstage, and application-owned output writeback via the read API. For direct control without going through ovstage, use the session write API (ovphysx_write). The legacy tensor bindings remain available for the same purpose but are deprecated.

The attachment is init-style. Call it once per instance, before any ovphysx_step(). Replacing the attached Stage requires successful completion of ovphysx_detach_ovstage() first.

Returns a task receipt. Execution may finish inline; admission success does not establish that attachment succeeded. Collect the task with ovphysx_wait_task() before using the attachment outside instance stream order. Earlier tasks finish execution first, without collecting their outcomes.

#include <ovphysx/ovphysx.h>

static ovphysx_enqueue_result_t attach_caller_owned_stage(
    ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
    ovstage_instance_t* stage,
    ovstage_ordinal_t read_ordinal)
{
    return ovphysx_attach_ovstage(handle, stage, read_ordinal);
}
Errors

Admission rejects an invalid handle, null stage, or zero read_ordinal with OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_ARGUMENT, and an already-attached instance or unavailable runtime API with OVPHYSX_API_ERROR. The schema guard also rejects admission with OVPHYSX_API_ERROR if ovstage reports a missing PhysX schema family after USD schema definitions were built, including by population or export, unless the guard is disabled (see below). Rejected receipts have no task identity; the schema guard takes no Stage ownership and changes no attachment. Runtime attach failures, including unreadable schema data and mismatched tolerance scales, belong to the accepted task and are reported by its wait.

Note

Not thread-safe per instance. Like the rest of the per-instance API, the caller must serialize ovphysx_attach_ovstage() against any other call on the same handle. The already-attached check and the attach are not internally locked against concurrent foreground callers.

Note

Each instance holds at most one live ovstage attach. Several instances may be attached at the same time. Attaching on one instance does not detach another. Detach or destroy only affects that instance’s attachment. The same ovstage instance cannot be attached twice. Process-wide limits still apply: one hard CPU-only mode, one SDK tolerance scale, and recording transitions that need every attached instance idle.

Note

The application owns schema registration. Separately install physx-usd-schemas and pass both module resource directories to ovstage_population_register_usd_schemas() before the first USD schema read, including population or export, in each process and worker. Population drops attributes of schemas it cannot resolve, including authored PhysX settings. This call checks both plugin families, physxSchema and omniUsdPhysicsDeformableSchema, once ovstage has built its USD schema registry. If ovstage reports either family missing, this and every later attach in the process fail by default. Restart and register before populating or exporting; late registration cannot repair the registry. A procedural Stage attached while USD schema definitions remain unbuilt skips the family check and leaves it active for later attaches. After population or export builds the definitions, the check applies even to procedural Stages. A registration another USD consumer made unobservable to ovstage cannot be detected. Nor can the guard identify schema families registered late before its first check: catching a late registration’s OVSTAGE_ERROR_OP_FAILED can let a later attach succeed with missing data. Always restart after a registration- ordering error; attach success does not prove schemas were available during population. The legacy create-time Carbonite setting /ovphysx/schemas/requireRegistration = false downgrades refusal to a warning and permits attach without repairing lost data; its default is true. The guard neither locates nor installs schema resources.

Note

Scenes that author Newton newton:* attributes also need the separately installed Newton USD schema (https://github.com/newton-physics/newton-usd-schemas) registered the same way; ovphysx reads those attributes as fallbacks for the PhysX spellings and does not ship that schema. Python’s PhysX.attach_ovstage() separately checks its registration and emits a warning when it cannot verify it. The C API performs no Newton check. The legacy create-time config entry /ovphysx/schemas/warnMissingNewtonSchema = false silences only the Python Newton warning, not the native PhysX registration guard.

Parameters:

  • handle – ovphysx instance handle.

  • stage – Caller-owned ovstage Stage (ovstage_instance_t*).

  • read_ordinal – Caller-owned ordinal at which the initial scan’s required physics data is sealed. Must be non-zero: 0 is reserved as the runtime’s internal “use payload attach-time ordinal” sentinel. The application owns ordinal advancement. Subsequent edits are drained via ovphysx_update_from_ovstage().

Pre:

handle is valid, ovphysx is not already attached to a Stage, stage is non-null, and read_ordinal is non-zero.

Pre:

stage and its sealed read_ordinal data remain valid through task completion. After successful attach, stage outlives the attachment, through successful detach completion. Destroying an attached Stage is undefined behavior. A failed attach may leave an attachment if rollback fails; check ovphysx_is_stage_attached() before releasing the Stage.

Post:

On successful task completion, subsequent ovphysx_update_from_ovstage() calls observe committed Stage writes through the runtime ovstage backend.

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t ovphysx_update_from_ovstage(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovstage_ordinal_range_t range,
)#

Pull and apply committed ovstage edits over an explicit ordinal range.

The caller is the producer that advanced ovstage ordinals and therefore owns the range boundaries, passed as ovstage’s own ovstage_ordinal_range_t. With has_start_ordinal == true the closed range [start_ordinal, end_ordinal] is drained. With has_start_ordinal == false only end_ordinal is drained (the single-ordinal form). The selected changes are drained through the active ovstage change feed and applied to the running simulation.

Returns a task receipt. The range value is copied; the caller-owned Stage and the selected sealed data must remain valid until task completion. Successful completion makes the updates visible to subsequent work. Earlier execution is drained without collecting its outcomes. This operation may execute inline; collect its own outcome with ovphysx_wait_task().

Ordinals at or below the latest successfully consumed ordinal are skipped. A range containing only consumed ordinals is a successful no-op. An overlapping range applies only its unread suffix. The initial read_ordinal is consumed by ovphysx_attach_ovstage(), so replaying it does not recreate the attach population or emit object-change notifications. Population authored and sealed at later ordinals is applied normally.

Errors

Admission rejects an invalid range or handle with OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_ARGUMENT, and a missing attachment or runtime API with OVPHYSX_API_ERROR. Runtime range drain failures belong to the accepted task. Failed updates need not be atomic; do not assume that no edits were applied or blindly replay the range.

Parameters:

  • handle – ovphysx instance handle.

  • range – ovstage ordinal range to drain (see ovstage_ordinal_range_t).

Pre:

handle is valid and the attach task completed successfully.

Pre:

when range.has_start_ordinal, range.start_ordinal <= range.end_ordinal.

Pre:

All selected writes are sealed by a completed write-floor operation covering range.end_ordinal. Waiting for ovstage_population_apply_usd_changes() only completes population. It does not advance the write floor.

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t ovphysx_detach_ovstage(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
)#

Detach the currently-attached ovstage Stage.

Returns a task receipt, including for an idempotent no-op on an unattached instance. Execution may finish inline; collect the outcome with ovphysx_wait_task(). Earlier execution finishes without collecting its outcomes. Successful task completion ends this instance’s Stage ownership. Keep the Stage alive until then, and longer if other users still own it. A failed detach can retain attachment ownership after partially retiring resources; ovphysx_is_stage_attached() is an ownership diagnostic, not a readiness check.

This is teardown, not restoration of initial poses. Instance configuration and the private simulation-time counter are preserved. Clears registered interests and any output-buffer registrations, so a subsequent ovphysx_attach_ovstage() to a different Stage starts clean. After detach, stage-dependent calls such as ovphysx_update_from_ovstage() and ovphysx_step() fail until a Stage is attached again. Detach invalidates the stage’s tensor and contact views. Do not read or write existing bindings. Destroy them and create replacements after attaching and realizing a stage again. Detach stops and finalizes an active OmniPVD recording started by this instance or when it removes the last live attachment. A peer-owned recording continues while another attachment remains live. After reattach, recording remains dormant until ovphysx_ovd_start_recording() is called.

Errors

Admission rejects invalid handles with OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_ARGUMENT. OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_STATE is retryable admission failure: attachment and write storage remain owned. Finish companion work or transitions and retry. Failures after teardown starts belong to the accepted task; collect them before deciding whether to retry or destroy the instance.

Parameters:

handle – ovphysx instance handle.

Pre:

handle is valid.

Post:

On successful task completion, ovphysx is unattached.

ovphysx_result_t ovphysx_is_stage_attached(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t instance_handle,
const void *stage,
bool *out_attached,
)#

Report whether this instance currently owns an attached stage.

Does not wait for simulation or validate existing resources, including resources from an earlier attachment of the same stage. This synchronous metadata snapshot neither creates a task nor collects outcomes. Wait for a lifecycle task first when its final state is needed. A false snapshot during pending attach does not permit Stage destruction, and true does not establish readiness. Serialize all calls on an instance.

Errors

  • OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_ARGUMENT if out_attached is NULL or instance_handle is invalid

Parameters:

  • instance_handle – ovphysx instance handle.

  • stage – NULL to check for any attachment, or a caller-owned stage pointer to compare with the current attachment. Never dereferenced.

  • out_attached – [out] True when a stage is attached and matches the supplied candidate (if any); false when detached, different, or on failure.

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t ovphysx_query(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovphysx_query_target_t object_type,
ovphysx_object_scope_t scope,
ovphysx_query_handle_t *out_query,
ovstage_query_result_t *out_summary,
)#

Open a query over the simulation’s output objects of one simulated type.

Mirrors the ovstage read idiom: the query is a handle (not a list). The matched prims come back per group at read time as the interned ovstage_read_group_t::prims.list (resolve via the attached Stage’s get_path_dictionary route or feed straight into the ovstage write path). Discover the produced attributes / total prim count with the optional query result. Pair every successful query with ovphysx_release_query.

An ovstage Stage must be attached (ovphysx_attach_ovstage).

Query, read, write, fetch, commit, and release return task receipts. The receipt reports admission only; wait for its task and check the task result before using outputs or starting an operation that depends on it. Keep input arrays, string storage, and output slots alive until task completion. These operations currently execute inline. The task contract does not promise that they will always finish before returning.

A successful task makes host outputs ready. CUDA columns retain the event contract below; task completion does not replace their readiness event. Rejected submissions have no task and do not consume resources. Accepted release submissions transfer cleanup to the SDK: stop using the resource immediately, even if waiting later reports failure. The SDK retains or quarantines storage whose safe release could not be established.

Resource handles belong to the instance that created them. A live handle from another instance returns OVPHYSX_API_NOT_FOUND. Releases of absent handles are successful no-ops when the supplied instance is valid.

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t ovphysx_query_selection(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovphysx_query_target_t object_type,
const ovphysx_query_selection_t *selection,
ovphysx_query_handle_t *out_query,
ovstage_query_result_t *out_summary,
)#

Open a query narrowed to a prim-set selection (ADR-0025).

Like ovphysx_query, but the objects of object_type are narrowed to selection &#8212; an explicit list of native prim-path handles OR a glob pattern &#8212; instead of a scope. The selection narrows BOTH the read and a write opened over the returned query &#8212; narrowing the query narrows the write, with no separate write-side call. A glob matches prims through the same resolver a tensor binding uses; an explicit list names prims directly by the handles the caller resolved. Either way the query keeps the objects of object_type whose prim is selected, and an OVPHYSX_QUERY_TARGET_ARTICULATION query also keeps each articulation one of whose links or joints is selected, as an articulation tensor binding does. Other types are not widened: OVPHYSX_QUERY_TARGET_RIGID_BODY does not cover articulation links (OVPHYSX_QUERY_TARGET_ARTICULATION_LINK does), and a link, joint or tendon query keeps only the members whose own prim is selected.

selection->pattern is an absolute path pattern (it starts with /), matched one path level per /-separated component: * and ? match within one name, ** spans any number of levels, and character classes and alternation pass through. The last component is searched at any depth below what the earlier components matched, unless it is a bare * or the pattern contains **. The complete rules, with examples, are on the “Path patterns” page of the ovphysx documentation (docs/read_write/path_patterns.md).

A selected query has no scope: it always covers every selected object of the type (the OVPHYSX_SCOPE_ALL set), including objects the solver did not move last step. It therefore stays valid across steps until a structural change, and a write opened over it never skips a selected object for being asleep. For only the objects that moved, use ovphysx_query with OVPHYSX_SCOPE_ACTIVE.

OVPHYSX_QUERY_TARGET_DEBUG_RENDER is not a prim set. This call rejects it with OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_ARGUMENT and “invalid object type”. Use ovphysx_query for that instance target.

selection is REQUIRED (non-NULL): the whole (type, scope) set is ovphysx_query. selection->prim_paths are interned ovx_primpath_t handles (see ovphysx_query_selection_t), NOT strings. prim_paths wins over pattern when both are set; they are never combined. A selection that resolves to no object of the queried type is a valid empty query &#8212; the optional query result reports total_prim_count == 0 and the first ovphysx_read fetch is end-of-iteration.

After acceptance, receipt.status is OVPHYSX_API_SUCCESS. Query construction failures are reported as OVPHYSX_API_ERROR by ovphysx_wait_task.

Errors

Rejection (receipt.status, no task):

  • OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_ARGUMENT if handle or object_type is invalid (including OVPHYSX_QUERY_TARGET_DEBUG_RENDER), out_query or selection is NULL, the selection provides neither prim_paths nor a pattern, prim_paths is NULL with a non-zero prim_paths_count, prim_paths contains OVX_INVALID_PRIMPATH, or the pattern does not start with /, contains an embedded NUL byte, or has a component exceeding the length limit.

  • OVPHYSX_API_ERROR if no ovstage is attached, the query backend is unavailable, pending simulation cannot be finished, or task creation fails.

Note

Selection narrows both the read and the write for every writable object type; a selected write that admits no prim of the queried type is a valid empty write, not an error.

Parameters:

  • handle – ovphysx instance handle.

  • object_type – Object type to query (see ovphysx_query).

  • selection – Prim-set selection (must be non-NULL; NULL returns OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_ARGUMENT).

  • out_query – [out] Nonzero and usable only after successful task completion.

  • out_summary – Optional creation-time discovery snapshot, as on ovphysx_query. Retain selection and output storage until task completion.

Returns:

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t (an enqueue receipt; wait on it with ovphysx_wait_task).

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t ovphysx_query_contacts(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
const ovphysx_contact_sensor_selection_t *selections,
uint32_t selection_count,
uint32_t filters_per_sensor,
ovphysx_query_handle_t *out_query,
ovstage_query_result_t *out_summary,
)#

Open a contact query: contact sensors with per-sensor filters (ADR-0044).

A OVPHYSX_QUERY_TARGET_CONTACT_SENSOR query whose rows are the bodies &#8212; and, on CPU simulation or GPU dynamics with CPU readback, colliders carrying PhysxContactReportAPI &#8212; the selections select, in selection order then match order, each paired with filters_per_sensor filter objects. Read it with ovphysx_read like any query. The filters are what the filtered contact attributes are measured against; the unfiltered ones (net forces) read the same on this query as on ovphysx_query.

Resolved once, when the query opens, with the contact binding’s rules: a body already matched by an earlier selection is not repeated, and each filter selection must match one object (shared by every sensor of its selection) or exactly one object per sensor (paired by position). Like the contact-sensor type, a selected body is a row only while it reports contacts (it or its articulation carries PhysxContactReportAPI); on CPU simulation or GPU dynamics with CPU readback a selected collider carrying the schema is a row too, host-only (a DirectGPU scene has no separate child-collider rows), and a body row overlaps its collider rows, so do not sum net forces or count contacts across them. A contact query has no scope, and a selection matching nothing adds no rows.

The schema on a separate child collider enables sensor selection, not reporting for its owning body. Enable reporting on the body, owning articulation link, or articulation root as well to avoid depending on reports from the other actor in each pair. The child remains a row but reads zero when neither actor reports matching contacts. Configure reporting settings on the reporting actor or articulation root. A standalone static collider is its own actor and enables reporting on CPU simulation and GPU dynamics with CPU readback; on DirectGPU its sensor row remains but reads zero force.

Errors

  • OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_ARGUMENT, before a task is created, if out_query or selections is NULL, selection_count is 0, a selection’s filters is NULL while filters_per_sensor is not 0, filters_per_sensor exceeds 21845, or any selection is invalid as for ovphysx_query_selection

  • OVPHYSX_API_ERROR if no ovstage is attached

  • OVPHYSX_API_ERROR, reported by ovphysx_wait_task, for a filter selection whose match count is neither 1 nor the selection’s sensor count, or a sensor whose filters name one object twice; the message names the selection, the filter and both counts

Parameters:

  • handle – ovphysx instance handle.

  • selections – selection_count sensor selections with their filters.

  • selection_count – Number of sensor selections (at least 1).

  • filters_per_sensor – Filter selections per sensor selection (0 for none, at most 21845).

  • out_query – [out] Nonzero and usable only after successful task completion.

  • out_summary – Optional creation-time discovery snapshot, as on ovphysx_query. Retain selections, their input buffers and output slots until task completion.

Returns:

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t (an enqueue receipt; wait on it with ovphysx_wait_task).

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t ovphysx_read(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovphysx_query_handle_t query,
const ovx_string_or_token_t *attributes,
size_t attribute_count,
ovphysx_read_handle_t *out_read,
ovphysx_read_result_t *out_summary,
)#

Read named output attributes for a query into typed column groups.

Opens a read session over query for the requested attributes, each given as an ovx_string_or_token_t: a string name (see OVPHYSX_ATTR_* in ovphysx_attributes.h) OR an interned token (e.g. from the optional query result, fed straight back with no token-to-string round-trip). Iterate the result with ovphysx_fetch_read_next, release each consumed group with ovphysx_release_group, and release the session with ovphysx_release_read. Names not produced by the queried type are skipped and reported in the optional summary. Duplicate canonical requests and unresolvable tokens fail the task; tokens take precedence over strings. Already-known backend failures fail open without publishing a session.

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t ovphysx_fetch_read_next(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovphysx_read_handle_t read,
const ovstage_read_group_t **out_group,
)#

Fetch the next output column group from a read session.

After successful task completion, *out_group points at the next ovstage_read_group_t, or is NULL at end of iteration. End of iteration is an ordinary successful task. A failed task leaves *out_group NULL and must not be treated as end of iteration. Keep out_group alive until completion.

The group is producer-owned (the caller does not allocate it): the returned ovstage_read_group_t pointer is a borrow valid until ovphysx_release_group is called for that group’s read_group_id, or the session is released.

Group lifetime (authoritative): the returned group struct and its stage-derived prims.list stay valid until ovphysx_release_group for that read_group_id (or ovphysx_release_read, which releases all). The numeric storage is owned by the read session instead: data.tensors, every tensor’s shape and data, prims.index_map, data.index_map, data.mask, and data.cuda_sync.wait_event stay valid until ovphysx_release_read. Fetching further groups and an intervening ovphysx_step do NOT invalidate either lifetime (the runtime gathers each column into session-owned storage at read time). Numeric snapshots also survive stage detach until session release or instance destruction. Detach invalidates the stage dictionary and its prim-list handles; do not resolve those handles after detaching.

A device (kDLCUDA) column additionally has a readiness contract: it is handed over before its producing work has necessarily completed. Wait on group.data.cuda_sync.wait_event before reading it from a non-default stream using CUDA’s cuStreamWaitEvent or cudaStreamWaitEvent. See ovphysx_read for the full rule. Validity and readiness are separate: the borrow above means the memory may still be read, the event means the values in it are final.

A failure already known during gathering fails read creation. A later fetch can still fail, for example if the attachment was invalidated. Check task completion before interpreting a NULL group as the end of iteration. Already-fetched numeric snapshots retain their session lifetime.

After acceptance, receipt.status is OVPHYSX_API_SUCCESS. Backend fetch failures are reported as OVPHYSX_API_ERROR by ovphysx_wait_task; end of iteration is successful completion with a NULL group.

Errors

Rejection (receipt.status, no task):

  • OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_ARGUMENT if handle is invalid or out_group is null.

  • OVPHYSX_API_NOT_FOUND if read is absent, released, or belongs to another instance.

  • OVPHYSX_API_ERROR if the read backend is unavailable or task creation fails.

Parameters:

  • handle – ovphysx instance handle.

  • read – Read-session handle from ovphysx_read.

  • out_group – [out] Receives a borrowed ovstage_read_group_t* for the next group (NULL at end of iteration or on error).

Returns:

Admission receipt. After successful task completion, NULL means done.

Pre:

handle and read are valid and out_group is non-null.

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t ovphysx_release_group(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovphysx_read_handle_t read,
ovstage_read_group_id_t group_id,
)#

Release one fetched group’s borrowed storage.

Releases the stage-derived prim-list storage pinned by ovphysx_fetch_read_next for group_id (an ovstage_read_group_t::read_group_id). After this the group struct and prims.list must not be dereferenced. Tensor, prim-index-map, data-index-map, mask, and CUDA-event storage belongs to the read session and remains valid until ovphysx_release_read.

Parameters:

  • handle – ovphysx instance handle.

  • read – Read-session handle the group came from.

  • group_id – The group’s ovstage_read_group_t::read_group_id.

Returns:

Admission receipt. Accepted release ends the group borrow immediately. An already-released or unknown id is a successful no-op.

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t ovphysx_release_read(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovphysx_read_handle_t read,
)#

Release a read session (and every borrowed group it still owns).

Finish all external CPU and CUDA consumers before submitting release or destroying the instance. The SDK waits for its own producing work before reclaiming device storage; it has no completion token for work launched by the caller. Accepted release ends all session borrows and transfers cleanup responsibility to the SDK.

Parameters:

  • handle – ovphysx instance handle.

  • read – Read-session handle from ovphysx_read.

Returns:

Admission receipt. An absent handle is a successful no-op for a valid instance. Wait to observe cleanup failures; do not retry accepted releases.

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t ovphysx_write(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovphysx_query_handle_t query,
const ovx_string_or_token_t *attributes,
size_t attribute_count,
ovphysx_write_handle_t *out_write,
ovphysx_write_result_t *out_summary,
)#

Open a write session for an array of named attributes.

The application-to-physics direction, the mirror of ovphysx_read. It reuses that query verbatim and adds no selection of its own: the session reaches exactly the set query matched, and there is no index, mask or prim-list parameter anywhere on this surface.

Each fetched group identifies its original request index through ovphysx_fetched_write_group_t::attribute_index, even when attributes have identical tensor shapes. Attributes are planned in request order. Commit order is chosen by the caller and no transactional rollback is provided. All names are validated before publishing a session. Canonical duplicates, including string/token aliases, and unsupported/read-only writes fail the creation task. A valid request with no matching objects is an empty session. Token ids take precedence over strings and must belong to the owning Stage dictionary; an unresolvable token fails rather than falling back to a string.

The write’s attribute vocabulary is its own: a name accepted here need not be one ovphysx_read emits, since write-only control inputs such as forces and wrenches have no read counterpart. Request attributes by semantic name; each fetched group’s request index identifies that name even when its storage is an instancer array.

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t ovphysx_fetch_write_next(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovphysx_write_handle_t write,
ovphysx_fetched_write_group_t *out_group,
)#

Fetch the next writable group from a write session.

After successful task completion, out_group->group points at the next ovstage_map_group_t, or is NULL at end of iteration. End of iteration is an ordinary successful task. A failed task leaves out_group->group NULL and must not be treated as end of iteration. Keep out_group alive until completion.

The group is producer-owned (the caller does not allocate it) and handed back as a const borrow. const is correct even on the write path: the group is a DESCRIPTOR the caller reads, describing BUFFERS the caller fills through data.tensors[i].data, which const permits since it does not propagate through pointer members. No field of the struct is the caller’s to assign, and tensor shape, dtype and device are dictated by the implementation.

Group storage stays valid until that group is committed or its write session is released, independent of further fetches. Detach and instance destruction retire write sessions. An intervening ovphysx_step does not invalidate a live group.

After acceptance, receipt.status is OVPHYSX_API_SUCCESS. Backend fetch failures are reported as OVPHYSX_API_ERROR by ovphysx_wait_task; end of iteration is successful completion with a NULL group.

Errors

Rejection (receipt.status, no task):

  • OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_ARGUMENT if handle is invalid or out_group is null.

  • OVPHYSX_API_NOT_FOUND if write is absent, released, or belongs to another instance.

  • OVPHYSX_API_ERROR if the write backend is unavailable or task creation fails.

Parameters:

  • handle – ovphysx instance handle.

  • write – Write-session handle from ovphysx_write.

  • out_group – [out] Receives the borrowed group and original request index. EOF is group == NULL and attribute_index == SIZE_MAX after successful task completion. Failed completion is never EOF.

Returns:

Admission receipt. After successful task completion, NULL means done.

Pre:

handle and write are valid and out_group is non-null.

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t ovphysx_commit_group(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovphysx_write_handle_t write,
const ovstage_map_group_t *group,
ovstage_cuda_sync_t write_done_sync,
)#

Commit a filled group, transferring ownership of its data to physics.

The caller must have filled EVERY mapped entry. There is no fill-mask, so a partially filled group publishes whatever its unfilled entries contain. To write fewer prims, query fewer. A live group belonging to this session is spent when accepted for publication, including when publication fails. Stop using its mapped pointers once the submission is accepted. A rejected submission leaves ownership with the caller. An invalid, foreign, or already-spent pointer fails the task without publishing or consuming another session’s group. Dereferencing them is undefined behavior rather than a checked error, since a raw data.tensors[i].data access makes no API call the runtime could reject.

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t ovphysx_release_write(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovphysx_write_handle_t write,
)#

Release a write session, discarding anything uncommitted.

Uncommitted groups are discarded. Finish all external CPU and CUDA work that fills those groups before submitting release: this call takes no producer completion token. Committed groups are not rolled back; the SDK waits for its own device work before reclaiming their storage. Once release is accepted, all session borrows end and cleanup belongs to the SDK, including after failure.

Parameters:

  • handle – ovphysx instance handle.

  • write – Write-session handle from ovphysx_write.

Returns:

Admission receipt. An absent handle is a successful no-op for a valid instance. Wait to observe cleanup failures; do not retry accepted releases.

ovphysx_result_t ovphysx_writability(
ovphysx_query_target_t object_type,
const ovx_string_or_token_t *attribute,
ovphysx_writability_t *out_writability,
)#

Ask whether an attribute can be written on an object type, and how.

The programmatic answer to a question that is otherwise only documented in prose, keyed on the SAME (object type, attribute) the write path takes (ovphysx_write resolves the object type through its query and names the attribute). This reports the API’s supported read/write vocabulary. Its scene-independent classification table is maintained separately and tested against runtime session admission.

Scene-independent: writability is a property of the write API, not of any live scene, so this needs no instance, query or step. A name the object type does not accept comes back OVPHYSX_WRITABILITY_UNCLASSIFIED, and ovphysx_write rejects it. Such a name is a gap to close, never an invitation to try the write anyway.

Errors

  • OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_ARGUMENT if out_writability or attribute is null, if attribute carries no string name (a token-only key), or if object_type is outside ovphysx_query_target_t (so an unknown type is distinguishable from a valid type that does not accept the name, which returns OVPHYSX_WRITABILITY_UNCLASSIFIED)

Parameters:

  • object_type – Object type the attribute would be written on (ovphysx_query’s selector), e.g. OVPHYSX_QUERY_TARGET_RIGID_BODY.

  • attribute – Attribute name (see the OVPHYSX_ATTR_* macros in ovphysx_attributes.h), as the string field of an ovx_string_or_token_t. STRING-ONLY: an interned-token-only key is rejected, because resolving a token needs a path dictionary this scene-free query does not have.

  • out_writability – [out] Receives the classification.

Returns:

ovphysx_result_t.

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t ovphysx_release_query(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovphysx_query_handle_t query,
)#

Release an output query.

Parameters:

  • handle – ovphysx instance handle.

  • query – Query handle from ovphysx_query.

Returns:

Admission receipt. An absent handle is a successful no-op for a valid instance. Wait to observe cleanup failures; do not retry accepted releases.

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t ovphysx_clone(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovphysx_string_t source_path_in_usd,
ovphysx_string_t *target_paths,
uint32_t num_target_paths,
const float *anchor_transforms,
const uint32_t *env_ids,
)#

Clone the subtree under the source path to one or more target paths in the internal physics representation (USD untouched).

The source path must exist in the stage. The target paths must not already exist in the stage.

Clones are created in the internal representation only (the USD file is not modified) and immediately participate in physics simulation. Backed by the PhysX SDK replicator, so cloned articulations are real articulations. Optimized for RL mass replication (1000s of instances). This is the clone entrypoint for both standalone callers and callers using an ovstage Stage (ovphysx_attach_ovstage).

#include <ovphysx/ovphysx.h>

static ovphysx_enqueue_result_t clone_two_environments(ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle)
{
    ovphysx_string_t targets[2] = {
        ovphysx_cstr("/World/env1"),
        ovphysx_cstr("/World/env2"),
    };
    return ovphysx_clone(
        handle, ovphysx_cstr("/World/env0"), targets, 2, NULL, NULL);
}
// To assemble one environment from several calls (heterogeneous ClonePlan), pass the same
// env_ids in each call so its objects share a runtime environment.
Side Effects

Adds live PhysX objects keyed by each target path. No USD or runtime-stage prims are authored.

Ownership

The target_paths array is read during the call. The caller retains ownership.

Errors

  • OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_ARGUMENT for invalid or duplicate targets, or a call after warmup / the first step

  • OVPHYSX_API_ERROR if no ovstage is attached or the clone fails

Note

Cross-environment collision isolation uses PhysX environment ids under GPU dynamics + GPU broadphase, controlled by /ovphysx/clone/useEnvIds (default on, per-process). The source holds env id 0 and clones get 1..N, so co-located clones (NULL anchor_transforms) are isolated from the source too. Environment ids do not isolate clones in CPU mode: co-located CPU clones share one collision space, so use spatially disjoint anchor_transforms. The runtime emits a warning through the Carbonite log stream when env ids are requested but GPU dynamics or GPU broadphase is unavailable. Register ovphysx_set_log_callback() to receive it programmatically. USD collision groups/filtering authored before cloning still work for finer control. Pass env_ids when one logical environment is assembled from several clone calls, so its objects share an id.

Note

Replication executes inline. An accepted task is already terminal when this call returns. ovphysx_wait_task() immediately collects its outcome.

Parameters:

  • handle – PhysX instance handle

  • source_path_in_usd – Path to the source subtree to clone (must exist)

  • target_paths – Array of target paths to clone to (must not exist)

  • num_target_paths – Number of target paths to clone to

  • anchor_transforms – Absolute world pose of each target subtree root. Entry i anchors the exact subtree at target_paths[i]. Flat [num_target_paths x 7] floats: (px, py, pz, qx, qy, qz, qw), quaternion imaginary-first (OVPHYSX_TENSOR_RIGID_BODY_POSE_F32, identity = (0,0,0,1)). Descendants keep their poses relative to the source subtree root (target_object_world = anchor_transforms[i] * inverse(source_root_world) * source_object_world). Pass NULL to co-locate every copy on the source. Co-location is collision-isolated only under GPU dynamics + GPU broadphase. Use spatially disjoint transforms in CPU mode.

  • env_ids – Optional logical environment id per target ([num_target_paths] uint32). Stable across calls: a shared id maps to one runtime environment (clones sharing it collide, isolated from others). Ids must be < 0x00FFFFFF (runtime id is env_ids[i] + 1). Pass NULL for automatic per-call numbering.

Returns:

Admission status and task identity. Rejection has zero identity; accepted execution failure is reported by a wait. On rejection, call ovphysx_get_last_error() on the same thread for the error message.

Pre:

handle must be valid.

Pre:

source_path_in_usd must exist and target_paths must be valid and unique.

Pre:

Must be called before ovphysx_warmup() or the first simulation step. Multiple ovphysx_clone() calls per attach are allowed in CPU and GPU mode while all of them precede warmup / first step. To clone after that point, use ovphysx_detach_ovstage() and reattach the source stage first. On GPU, cloning later would reallocate DirectGPU buffers and corrupt initialized state.

Post:

Cloned physics objects are live when the accepted task succeeds.

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t ovphysx_step(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
float step_dt,
)#

Enqueue an asynchronous physics simulation step.

The simulation time is tracked internally. Each step advances it by step_dt. The timestep is passed through without clamping or substepping. The caller is responsible for choosing a timestep appropriate for the simulation.

PhysX CUDA-context failures after admission are reported by the task wait, with a retained CUDA diagnostic even when logging is disabled.

Side Effects

Mutates physics state and may trigger internal events and callbacks.

Threading

Must not be called concurrently on the same instance without external synchronization.

Errors

  • OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_ARGUMENT for invalid inputs

  • OVPHYSX_API_ERROR for internal failures

#include <ovphysx/ovphysx.h>

static ovphysx_enqueue_result_t step_one_frame(ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle)
{
    return ovphysx_step(handle, 1.0f / 60.0f);
}
Parameters:

  • handle – ovphysx instance

  • step_dt – Finite, nonnegative simulation timestep in seconds

Returns:

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t with admission status and instance/task identity

Pre:

handle must be a valid instance handle.

Post:

Simulation advances by step_dt when the op completes.

ovphysx_result_t ovphysx_step_sync(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
float step_dt,
)#

Synchronous step: simulate one physics timestep and wait for completion in a single call.

This step does not create a task receipt. Earlier asynchronous work is completed first, without collecting its outcomes. Those receipts remain available to ovphysx_wait_task() or ovphysx_wait_all().

Use this whenever the caller steps and immediately waits for results, that is, does not overlap GPU simulation with CPU work between dispatch and fetch.

The simulation time is tracked internally. Each step advances it by step_dt.

Parameters:

  • handle – Physics instance handle.

  • step_dt – Finite, nonnegative timestep [s], passed through as in ovphysx_step().

Returns:

ovphysx_result_t with OVPHYSX_API_SUCCESS on success. A PhysX CUDA-context error returns OVPHYSX_API_ERROR; retrieve its diagnostic with ovphysx_get_last_error(), even when logging is disabled. A recoverable capacity-overflow report alone does not fail the call.

ovphysx_result_t ovphysx_warmup(ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle)#

Explicitly run the warmup step (optional, synchronous).

On first use, a real simulation step with a minimal timestep (~1ns) is run to initialize PhysX structures and disable per-step Fabric sync overhead. This is done automatically by legacy tensor-binding reads (auto-warmup). Session reads through ovphysx_read() do not auto-warm; call this explicitly to control when the latency occurs.

Works in both CPU and GPU mode. In GPU mode, this also populates DirectGPU buffers.

IMPORTANT: The warmup advances simulation state (positions may change infinitesimally). It is NOT a “dry run”. For deterministic initial conditions, call this before reading initial tensor state.

This function is idempotent. Calling it multiple times has no effect after the first successful call (per stage). Warmup state resets when the stage changes through detach and attach.

#include <ovphysx/ovphysx.h>

static ovphysx_result_t warm_up_instance(ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle)
{
    return ovphysx_warmup(handle);
}
Side Effects

Advances simulation by a minimal timestep on first call. Disables per-step Fabric sync (enabling direct TensorAPI mode).

Errors

  • OVPHYSX_API_ERROR for internal failures

Parameters:

handle – Instance handle

Returns:

ovphysx_result_t

Pre:

handle must be valid.

Post:

Warmup completed for the active stage.

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t ovphysx_update_articulations_kinematic(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovphysx_query_handle_t query,
uint32_t flags,
)#

Recompute articulation link transforms and/or velocities for the whole articulations selected by a physics-output query, without running a normal simulation step.

The query must select OVPHYSX_QUERY_TARGET_ARTICULATION. A query from ovphysx_query_selection updates only the articulations its selection names, through their root, a link or a joint; every other articulation is left unchanged.

The returned receipt reports admission. Wait for successful task completion before reading the updated link state. The update currently executes inline. It is useful after writing articulation DOF positions (through the session write API, ovphysx_write, or the deprecated tensor bindings) and before reading link pose tensors in the same frame.

NOTE: On the first GPU kinematic update after loading USD, an automatic warmup simulation step may be performed to initialize PhysX structures. See the tensor auto-warmup note in ovphysx_legacy.h.

Once GPU warmup is complete, the FK refresh itself does not run collision detection, integration, solver work, or contact generation.

Parameters:

  • handle – Physics instance handle.

  • query – Live query owned by handle and selecting OVPHYSX_QUERY_TARGET_ARTICULATION. Membership is evaluated when the task executes.

  • flags – Bitwise OR of ovphysx_articulation_kinematic_flag_t. Zero is a successful no-op after validating the query. Non-DirectGPU scenes honor the component mask. DirectGPU’s native refresh may update both components for either supported nonzero mask.

Returns:

Admission receipt. Lazy attach, warmup, and backend failures are reported by waiting for the accepted task.

ovphysx_result_t ovphysx_subscribe_object_changes(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
const ovphysx_object_change_callbacks_t *callbacks,
ovphysx_subscription_id_t *out_subscription,
)#

Native PhysX addresses are the read-only physxPointer column (OVPHYSX_ATTR_PHYSX_POINTER).

Query the matching ovphysx_query_target_t and read that attribute. There is no dedicated pointer lookup. Subscribe to PhysX object create/destroy notifications.

Pair with a physxPointer read to manage the lifetime of cached PhysX SDK pointers. On a destruction notification the caller MUST drop the cached pointer before returning from the callback; it is unusable after that return. On a bulk teardown the caller MUST drop every cached pointer before returning from the all-objects callback. On a creation notification the caller should mark the prim path as dirty in its own cache and read physxPointer for the new address ONLY after the triggering synchronous call returns, or after ovphysx_wait_task() returns for async work, never from inside the callback itself (see Threading below).

Subscriptions are per-instance. Callbacks fire only while this handle’s own attachment is live. A peer instance does not receive this instance’s events, and cannot unsubscribe this instance’s subscription.

Lifecycle: callbacks fire for changes that occur during simulation and ovphysx_detach_ovstage()’s bulk teardown. The initial object population from ovstage attach/update is NOT notified, since the caller already has that state from setup. ovphysx_clone() does NOT fire object_created notifications. Pointer caches that need to track cloned objects must be refreshed after ovphysx_wait_task() returns on the clone operation. These notifications stay callbacks; they are not query or read records.

Threading: callbacks may fire from internal worker threads. Do NOT call other ovphysx APIs from inside a callback. Defer that until the triggering synchronous call returns, or until ovphysx_wait_task() returns for async work. See the docstring on ovphysx_object_change_callbacks_t for the full contract.

Failure modes:

  • OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_ARGUMENT if callbacks or out_subscription is NULL, or if every callback function pointer in the struct is NULL.

  • OVPHYSX_API_ERROR if the physics runtime is not available (e.g. no ovphysx instance has been created yet).

On failure, *out_subscription is set to OVPHYSX_INVALID_SUBSCRIPTION_ID.

Parameters:

  • handle – [in] Instance that owns the subscription.

  • callbacks – [in] Pointer to the callback set. The struct is copied internally, so the caller does not need to keep it alive after this call returns.

  • out_subscription – [out] Receives the subscription ID on success. Pass this to ovphysx_unsubscribe_object_changes() to stop receiving notifications.

Returns:

OVPHYSX_API_SUCCESS on success, or an error status.

ovphysx_result_t ovphysx_unsubscribe_object_changes(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovphysx_subscription_id_t subscription,
)#

Unsubscribe from PhysX object change notifications.

Stops delivery of further notifications for the given subscription ID. OVPHYSX_API_SUCCESS does not return while one of this subscription’s callbacks is still running. After that return the subscription ID is consumed and must not be reused, and user_data will not be touched again by this subscription.

Calling this from inside any object-change callback returns OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_STATE and leaves the subscription active. That check follows the Carbonite task when the callback is running as one, and the native thread otherwise. Another task on the same worker is not inside the callback. The dispatch snapshot retains every subscriber until that callback returns, so waiting would deadlock. Unsubscribe again after it returns.

Idempotency: passing an already-unsubscribed or unknown subscription ID returns OVPHYSX_API_NOT_FOUND. A subscription owned by another instance also returns OVPHYSX_API_NOT_FOUND and leaves that subscription active. OVPHYSX_INVALID_SUBSCRIPTION_ID is rejected with OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_ARGUMENT. NOT_FOUND is not a drain barrier: only SUCCESS means in-flight callbacks for that subscription have finished.

Parameters:

  • handle – Instance that owns the subscription.

  • subscription – Subscription ID returned from ovphysx_subscribe_object_changes().

Returns:

OVPHYSX_API_SUCCESS on success, or an error status.

ovphysx_result_t ovphysx_wait_task(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovphysx_enqueue_result_t task,
ovphysx_timeout_t timeout_ns,
ovphysx_wait_task_result_t *out_wait_result,
)#

Collect the terminal outcome of one accepted task.

Reports and acknowledges only the given task, including when earlier work must finish to preserve execution ordering. Uncollected failures of other tasks remain available to their own wait or ovphysx_wait_all(). A terminal outcome is single-use; another wait returns NOT_FOUND. Timeout leaves the unfinished task retryable and returns its receipt in pending_task.

The timeout bounds readiness. Zero polls once; OVPHYSX_TIMEOUT_INFINITE waits indefinitely. Readiness observed at the deadline wins. Synchronous finalization can extend wall-clock duration beyond the readiness timeout.

#include <ovphysx/ovphysx.h>

static ovphysx_result_t collect_task(
    ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle, ovphysx_enqueue_result_t task)
{
    ovphysx_wait_task_result_t result = {0};
    ovphysx_result_t status = ovphysx_wait_task(
        handle, task, OVPHYSX_TIMEOUT_INFINITE, &result);
    ovphysx_destroy_wait_task_result(&result);
    return status;
}
Ownership

Failed receipts and borrowed messages belong to out_wait_result until ovphysx_destroy_wait_task_result(). Do not modify the returned fields, free error_tasks separately, or shallow-copy the result. Allocation failure leaves an empty destructible output and terminal outcomes uncollected, so callers can retry.

Threading

Calls on one instance must be externally serialized, including waits and error lookup. Serialized calls may move between threads.

Parameters:

  • handle – Owning instance. Validated before other arguments.

  • task – Copyable successful-admission receipt from a task producer.

  • timeout_ns – Readiness timeout in nanoseconds.

  • out_wait_result – [out] Non-null zero-initialized result. Nonempty reuse is rejected without overwriting it. Destroy after processing.

Returns:

SUCCESS for successful completion, ERROR for an execution or internal failure, TIMEOUT for unfinished work, INVALID_ARGUMENT for a zero/rejected/wrong-instance receipt or invalid output, NOT_FOUND for an invalid instance or a never-issued/already-collected task.

ovphysx_result_t ovphysx_wait_all(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovphysx_timeout_t timeout_ns,
ovphysx_wait_task_result_t *out_wait_result,
)#

Collect uncollected tasks accepted at call entry, in submission order.

Uses one readiness deadline for the entire call. Stops at the earliest unfinished task when that deadline expires; later outcomes stay uncollected. Earlier completed failures are returned in error_tasks even on TIMEOUT, which takes precedence over ERROR. Successful terminal outcomes are collected too. A discarded original receipt does not discard its failure. Empty and repeated wait-all calls succeed when no uncollected task remains.

Validation, ownership and timeout rules match ovphysx_wait_task(). An all-zero pending_task means no task remains pending within this call’s cutoff.

ovphysx_string_t ovphysx_get_last_error(void)#

Query the error string for the last failed API call on the calling thread.

The returned string is valid until the next ovphysx API call on the same thread. Returns a stable empty string if the last call succeeded.

#include <ovphysx/ovphysx.h>
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    ovphysx_result_t result = ovphysx_initialize();
    if (result.status != OVPHYSX_API_SUCCESS) {
        ovphysx_string_t error = ovphysx_get_last_error();
        if (error.length != 0)
            fprintf(stderr, "Error: %.*s\n", (int)error.length, error.ptr);
        return 1;
    }
    return ovphysx_shutdown().status == OVPHYSX_API_SUCCESS ? 0 : 1;
}
Threading

Thread-local storage. Safe to call from any thread.

Returns:

Error message, or {“”, 0} on success. ptr is always non-NULL and ptr[length] is ‘\0’.

ovphysx_string_t ovphysx_get_last_task_error(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovphysx_enqueue_result_t task,
)#

Borrow a collected task’s error from its live wait-result.

Lookup is read-only and never acknowledges work. A missing retained cause returns {“”, 0}. An invalid instance or zero/rejected/wrong-instance receipt also sets the immediate diagnostic retrieved by ovphysx_get_last_error(). The string survives unrelated waits and instance destruction until the owning wait-result is destroyed. A fresh lookup requires a live instance. ptr is always non-NULL and ptr[length] is ‘\0’.

void ovphysx_destroy_wait_task_result(
ovphysx_wait_task_result_t *result,
)#

Release wait-result storage and zero every field.

Accepts NULL and already-cleaned results. Safe after instance teardown; retained messages and receipts own no simulation or CUDA resources. A non-NULL result must be zero-initialized or produced by a task wait with its returned fields unchanged. Never free error_tasks separately.

ovphysx_result_t ovphysx_set_log_callback(
ovphysx_log_level_t min_severity,
const ovphysx_string_t *channel_filter,
ovphysx_log_callback_t callback,
void *user_data,
)#

Set or disable the application log callback.

One callback may be registered. Calling again publishes the replacement for newly accepted messages, then waits for the prior registration’s in-flight invocations before returning. Passing NULL for callback immediately stops accepting delivery and drains the prior registration. Once set, the callback pointer and resources reachable through user_data must remain valid until a later replacing or disabling call, or a successful ovphysx_shutdown(), returns. This includes shutdown with live handles retained only for explicit destruction. During replacement, accepted invocations of the old registration may overlap invocations of the newly published registration. Invocations within each registration remain serialized. min_severity applies to every record in the observed process log stream. Records from the library-owned omni_physx_sdk, omni.physx, and ovphysx_internal sources are also subject to the source threshold configured by OVPHYSX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_LOG_LEVEL. OVPHYSX_LOG_DEFAULT uses WARNING.

channel_filter is optional. It is a comma-separated list of channel=level rules. ASCII whitespace around entries, channels, and levels is ignored, and level names are case-insensitive. A rule matches any channel beginning with its raw prefix. Rules are considered in declaration order. The longest matching prefix wins, and a later rule wins ties between equal-length matching prefixes. An empty filter uses min_severity for every channel.

Note

The callback may be invoked from any thread, but invocations for the active registration are serialized.

Note

The callback observes Carbonite’s process log stream. The channel parameter identifies the emitting source for application filtering.

Note

Must not be called from within the callback. Returns OVPHYSX_API_ERROR if called during callback dispatch.

Note

An OVPHYSX_API_ERROR after valid arguments may be reported after the replacement was published. Conservatively keep callback and user_data alive until a later successful replace, disable, or shutdown drains the slot.

Parameters:

  • min_severity – Minimum delivered severity.

  • channel_filter – Optional non-owning filter view, copied by the call.

  • callback – Callback function, or NULL to disable.

  • user_data – Opaque pointer forwarded to every callback invocation.

Returns:

ovphysx_result_t with status.

Post:

Invalid arguments leave the prior registration unchanged.

ovphysx_result_t ovphysx_flush_log(ovphysx_timeout_t timeout_ns)#

Wait for application-callback deliveries accepted before this call.

This is an exact barrier for records already handed to ovphysx by Carbonite. If the host enabled Carbonite asynchronous logging, records still buffered upstream have not yet been accepted and are outside this barrier. Successful ovphysx_shutdown() flushes that upstream buffer before disabling and draining the callback.

Parameters:

timeout_ns – Maximum wait in nanoseconds. OVPHYSX_TIMEOUT_POLL polls. OVPHYSX_TIMEOUT_INFINITE waits indefinitely.

Returns:

OVPHYSX_API_SUCCESS when drained, OVPHYSX_API_TIMEOUT on timeout, or OVPHYSX_API_ERROR when called from a log callback.

Geometry Queries#

Questions asked of the scene’s collision geometry at your own inputs. Declared in ovphysx_geometry_query.h; include it alongside ovphysx.h, which does not include it.

Use ovphysx_evaluate_sdf_shapes() to evaluate signed distance fields at your own points. Pass a live OVPHYSX_QUERY_TARGET_SDF_SHAPE query, a points tensor [N, Q, 3] and an output tensor [N, Q, 4] (gradient, then signed distance), float32 on the scene’s CUDA device, plus the producer handoff for the points, as for ovphysx_commit_group. The output is written when the task completes. The Python method is PhysX.evaluate_sdf_shapes(), which opens and releases the query itself and waits internally; the experimental C++ wrapper is PhysX::evaluateSdfShapes(). See SDF shapes for rows, frame and device requirements.

Functions

ovphysx_enqueue_result_t ovphysx_evaluate_sdf_shapes(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovphysx_query_handle_t query,
const DLTensor *points,
DLTensor *out,
ovstage_cuda_sync_t points_ready,
)#

Evaluate the signed distance fields of the SDF shapes a query selects.

The successor of the deprecated SDF view (ovphysx_create_sdf_view / ovphysx_evaluate_sdf), on the session query. Open the query with type OVPHYSX_QUERY_TARGET_SDF_SHAPE: its rows are the collision shapes the SDF view accepts &#8212; a prim carrying PhysicsCollisionAPI and PhysxSDFMeshCollisionAPI whose shape is a triangle mesh with an SDF, runtime clones included. A query from ovphysx_query_selection orders its rows as its selection: explicit prim handles in the order given, a pattern in the same matcher order the SDF view used; a whole-set query orders them as the runtime stores them. A selected prim that is not an SDF shape is skipped, with a warning, as the SDF view skipped it.

For each row i and point j, out[i][j] receives the gradient (x, y, z) and then the signed distance at points[i][j], negative inside. Points and gradients are in the shape’s mesh-local space &#8212; the unscaled frame of the mesh’s vertices &#8212; and no transform is applied. Q, the points per shape, is read from the tensors on every call. A point outside the shape’s SDF grid (the mesh bounds padded by the SDF margin) is evaluated, not refused, as by the SDF view: its distance is the SDF value at the nearest grid point plus the distance to the grid, a positive upper bound, and its gradient points away from the shape.

Evaluation needs a DirectGPU scene, all the rows in one scene, at most 65535 rows &#8212; PhysX launches its SDF evaluation with one CUDA grid row per shape &#8212; and at most 2^31 - 1 points in all (N x Q), which PhysX indexes in 32-bit arithmetic. It also needs the scene to have simulated since its physics objects were last created or released, because PhysX uploads shape data to the GPU only when it simulates. On the first evaluation after loading USD, an automatic warmup simulation step may be performed, as for the SDF view; after that the call never steps, so step once after such a change before evaluating. out is complete once the task has completed.

ovphysx_result_t ovphysx_create_tensor_binding(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
const ovphysx_tensor_binding_desc_t *desc,
ovphysx_tensor_binding_handle_t *out_binding_handle,
)#

Create a tensor binding for bulk data access (synchronous).

A tensor binding connects a physics-object path pattern (e.g., “/World/robot*”) to a tensor type (e.g., OVPHYSX_TENSOR_RIGID_BODY_POSE_F32), enabling efficient bulk read/write of physics data for all matching objects. Runtime-only clone paths are eligible even when no USD prim is authored at the path. Each call returns an independent handle. Destroying one binding does not invalidate another binding for the same objects. A new binding selects the currently eligible realized objects even while older bindings remain alive.

If the pattern matches zero physics objects, the binding is still created successfully with element_count = 0. This lets callers treat optional scene content as an empty current result instead of an error. Empty bindings do not update when matching physics objects are added or recreated. Destroy the old binding and create a new one after topology changes.

Binding lifetime is tied to the currently realized physics objects. The application owns the stage lifecycle: if it will call ovphysx_detach_ovstage(), remove USD data containing bound objects, or otherwise replace/reparse the stage so those objects are destroyed and recreated, cached bindings should be destroyed before the lifecycle operation when practical. If a stale binding survives, only destroy it. Do not read or write through it. Create replacement bindings after the operation completes. ovphysx_step() and ovphysx_step_sync() do not invalidate bindings.

#include <ovphysx/ovphysx_legacy.h>

static ovphysx_result_t create_pose_binding(
    ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
    ovphysx_tensor_binding_handle_t* out_binding)
{
    ovphysx_tensor_binding_desc_t desc = {
        .pattern = OVPHYSX_LITERAL("/World/robot*"),
        .tensor_type = OVPHYSX_TENSOR_RIGID_BODY_POSE_F32,
    };
    return ovphysx_create_tensor_binding(handle, &desc, out_binding);
}
Diagnostics

Pattern bindings quiet expected TensorAPI no-match diagnostics on the simulation view used to create that binding. Explicit prim_paths keep the default error-level no-match diagnostics for typo detection. For programmatic partial-miss checks with explicit prim_paths, compare the requested paths with ovphysx_tensor_binding_get_prim_paths().

Threading

Do not create bindings concurrently with stage mutation.

Side Effects

Allocates internal binding resources.

Errors

  • OVPHYSX_API_INVALID_ARGUMENT for invalid inputs

  • OVPHYSX_API_ERROR for internal failures

Deprecated:

The tensor-binding API is deprecated. Use ovphysx_read (reads) and ovphysx_write (writes) instead.

Parameters:

  • handle – Instance handle

  • desc – Binding descriptor with pattern and tensor_type

  • out_binding_handle – [out] Binding handle on success

Returns:

ovphysx_result_t (synchronous - completes before returning)

Pre:

handle, desc, and out_binding_handle must be valid.

Post:

Binding handle retains native resources until explicitly destroyed via ovphysx_destroy_tensor_binding(), or until the parent instance is destroyed. Stage detach or bound-object removal invalidates the underlying TensorAPI view. Destroy stale bindings and create replacements after the lifecycle operation completes.

ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,

Destroy a tensor binding and release associated resources (synchronous).

Parameters:

Returns:

ovphysx_result_t

Post:

ovphysx_result_t ovphysx_get_tensor_binding_spec(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovphysx_tensor_binding_handle_t binding_handle,
ovphysx_tensor_spec_t *out_spec,
)#

Get the tensor layout specification for a binding.

Returns dtype, ndim, and shape needed to allocate a compatible DLTensor. This is the preferred API for constructing DLTensors correctly.

NOTE: ovphysx_tensor_spec_t stores shape in a fixed-size int64[4] for a stable C ABI. Only the first ndim entries are meaningful. The remaining entries are always set to 0.

See ovphysx_tensor_type_t documentation for shapes, dtype, and layouts per tensor type. Layout is always row-major contiguous (C-order). Most bindings are float32. OVPHYSX_TENSOR_DEFORMABLE_SIM_ELEMENT_INDICES_S32 is int32.

    ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
    ovphysx_tensor_binding_handle_t binding,

{

}

None.

Errors

Returns:

ovphysx_result_t

ovphysx_result_t ovphysx_get_tensor_binding_native_device(
ovphysx_instance_handle_t handle,
ovphysx_tensor_binding_handle_t binding_handle,
DLDevice *out_device,
)#

Get the native device used by a tensor binding.

Returns the device used by the binding’s native TensorAPI read/write path: DLDevice{kDLCPU, 0} for host-resident bindings, or DLDevice{kDLCUDA, device_ordinal} for CUDA-resident bindings. CPU-only property tensors report CPU even when the simulation runs on CUDA. For kDLCUDA, device_id is the process-visible CUDA runtime ordinal used with cudaSetDevice() or a framework device such as cuda:N, not a physical PCI bus index.

This reports native residency, not every device accepted by read/write. Using the native device avoids staging when another accepted placement would require it. The value remains stable for the lifetime of a live binding. Unlike the layout-only spec getter, this is a live mapping query and rejects an invalidated simulation view.

{

}

None.
